_note: Rubric from fixtures/debug-test/expected-findings.md. Default mode (no --flake/--drift): the root cause is a missing `await` on a Playwright web-first assertion, caught at Step 2 (quick QA heuristics) → 🟢 High confidence + a local fix, NO routing to the Playwright healer or diagnosing-bugs. `anchors` exist only for the offline heuristic judge; the LLM judge grades `claim` directly.

must_surface.claim: Root cause is a missing `await` on a Playwright web-first (async, auto-retrying) assertion.
Explains the consequence: unawaited, the assertion is a floating promise that never settles, so it can never fail (false positive).
Proposes the fix: await the assertion — `await expect(banner).toBeVisible()`.

must_not.claim: Must NOT route to the Playwright healer — this is not a locator/selector/timeout error.
Must NOT route to diagnosing-bugs — the quick heuristics resolve it at Step 2.

cases._note: Step 4.5 (#190, ADR-0047 §2). Rubric from fixtures/debug-test/expected-findings.md → 'Step 4.5 heal classification', Case 1. Sample-graded only (no fixture_files, no isolated workspace): reaching this step live needs an initialized Playwright healer that actually edits the spec, which the offline lane can't stage — same lane as the qa-compass routing cases. The riskiest claim — a healer that rewrote an expected literal must NOT collapse into 'done' — is what the rubric locks.

must_surface.claim: Buckets the heal as expected-value: the healer changed an assertion's expected literal, not a selector or a wait.
Shows the assertion diff it classified from — the old → new expected value.
Routes the expected-value bucket to audit-test's baseline-lock check instead of clearing the heal.
Reports the baseline-lock verdict inline before calling the heal done.
Proposes a `Healed-by: debug-test` commit trailer.
States the trailer block is proposed for a human or a commit template to apply, not written by this skill.

must_not.claim: Must NOT report the healer's pass as done on the strength of the pass alone.
Must NOT claim to have created or amended the commit carrying the heal.

cases._note: Rubric from fixtures/debug-test/expected-findings.md → 'Step 4.5 heal classification', Case 2. Sample-graded only, same reason as the case above. The cheap bucket, locked deliberately: a locator-only heal must stay cheap (no mutation, no audit-test hop) AND still emit a trailer, because 'the same spec healed four times for a locator' is exactly the repeat-heal pattern #194 reads.

must_surface.claim: Buckets the heal as selector/wait only.
Clears the heal without spending a mutation on it.
Still proposes the commit trailer for this cheap bucket.

must_not.claim: Must NOT route a locator-only heal to audit-test — that spends a mutation on the low-risk common case.
Must NOT suppress the trailer for the cheap bucket.

cases._note: Step 4.6 (#194, ADR-0047 §2 read side). Rubric from fixtures/debug-test/expected-findings.md → 'Step 4.6 repeat-heal check', Case 3. Sample-graded only, same reason as the Step 4.5 cases: reaching Step 4.6 needs a real multi-commit git history of prior heals, which the offline fixture lane can't stage. Locks the bucket-accurate reading: three same-bucket heals inside the window, all carrying the Heal-bucket trailer, must surface as a named 🔁 repeat-heal, not disappear because each individual heal was the cheap locator bucket.

must_surface.claim: Reads the file's prior heal history via `git log --follow` within a 90-day window.
States the reading is bucket-accurate — every commit touching the file in the window carried a `Heal-bucket` trailer.
Names the count (3) and the bucket (locator) in the finding.
Emits the 🔁 repeat-heal finding rather than treating three cheap-bucket heals as nothing worth reporting.

must_not.claim: Must NOT report 'no repeats' — three locator heals on the same file inside the window is exactly the pattern this check exists to surface.
Must NOT claim this required writing a ledger, store, or cache file.

cases._note: Step 4.6 (#194, ADR-0047 §2 read side). Rubric from fixtures/debug-test/expected-findings.md → 'Step 4.6 repeat-heal check', Case 4. Sample-graded only, same reason as above. Locks the degradation ladder's other end: when no commit in the window carries a Heal-bucket trailer, the check must fall back to a plain file-churn count, label it explicitly as the weaker signal, and still report it — never read an all-trailerless history as 'no repeats' (the failure mode #194's acceptance criteria names directly).

must_surface.claim: Finds zero commits carrying a `Heal-bucket` trailer in the window — a churn-only reading.
Falls back to a plain file-churn count with no bucket breakdown.
States the edit count (4) found in the window.
Labels the churn fallback explicitly as the weaker signal.

must_not.claim: Must NOT report 'no repeats' or 'clean' just because trailers are absent — an untrailered history is a weaker read, not a clean one.
Must NOT invent a bucketed repeat-heal count for commits that carry no trailer.
